outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The cohort consisted of mothers delivered by Crash Caesarean Section (CCS) in a busy tertiary maternity unit over a four-week period.
finding: The audit revealed that all Crash Caesarean Sections (CCS) were performed within the recommended 30 minutes, averaging 10.2 minutes, but also identified 15 maternal complications, 1 birth injury, and 4 perinatal deaths among the cases.
mod_finding: All Crash Caesarean Sections were performed within the recommended 30 minutes with a mean decision to delivery interval of 10.2 minutes, and the most common indications included non-reassuring fetal status, cord prolapse, and placental abruption.
